questions.stem: The products of aerobic respiration in a muscle cell are
questions.explanation: With oxygen available, glucose is broken down completely, so its carbon leaves as carbon dioxide and its hydrogen combines with oxygen to give water. Complete breakdown is why aerobic respiration releases so much more energy than the anaerobic route.

distractorRationale.a: Ethanol and carbon dioxide are the products of anaerobic respiration in yeast
distractorRationale.b: Lactic acid is the product of anaerobic respiration in muscle
distractorRationale.d: Glucose and oxygen are the reactants, and they are also the products of photosynthesis

questions.stem: Anaerobic respiration in yeast produces
questions.explanation: Yeast carries out alcoholic fermentation, splitting glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide. Both products are put to use by people: the carbon dioxide makes bread dough rise and the ethanol gives palm wine and beer their alcohol.

distractorRationale.a: Lactic acid is produced by animal muscle and some bacteria, not by yeast
distractorRationale.c: Carbon dioxide and water are the products of aerobic, not anaerobic, respiration
distractorRationale.d: Oxygen and glucose are products of photosynthesis

questions.stem: Aerobic respiration releases far more energy per molecule of glucose than anaerobic respiration because in aerobic respiration

options.text: glucose is broken down completely, so no energy remains locked in the products
the reaction happens at a higher temperature

questions.explanation: Ethanol and lactic acid are still energy-rich molecules, so anaerobic respiration leaves most of the glucose's chemical energy unused. Aerobic respiration oxidises the glucose all the way to carbon dioxide and water, extracting roughly twenty times as much energy.

distractorRationale.a: The comparison is made per molecule of glucose, so the quantity used is not the reason
distractorRationale.c: Both processes occur at normal body temperature
distractorRationale.d: Oxygen carries no energy of its own; it acts as the final acceptor of hydrogen

questions.stem: A sprinter continues to breathe deeply for several minutes after finishing a race. This is mainly to

options.text: supply oxygen to oxidise the lactic acid that accumulated in the muscles
remove ethanol produced in the muscles
replace the glucose used during the race

questions.explanation: During the race the muscles respired partly anaerobically and built up lactic acid. Removing that acid requires oxygen, either to oxidise it to carbon dioxide and water or to convert it back to glucose in the liver, and this required extra oxygen is the oxygen debt.

distractorRationale.a: Cooling is achieved mainly by sweating and vasodilation of skin vessels
distractorRationale.c: Muscle produces lactic acid, not ethanol; ethanol is a yeast product
distractorRationale.d: Glucose is replaced from liver glycogen and from food, not by breathing

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes respiration from combustion?

options.text: Respiration occurs in many small enzyme-controlled steps at body temperature, while combustion is a single rapid reaction at high temperature
Respiration produces carbon dioxide, while combustion does not
Combustion requires enzymes, while respiration does not
Respiration releases light, while combustion does not

questions.explanation: Both processes oxidise a fuel and both give out carbon dioxide and energy, so the true differences lie in how the energy is released. Respiration is a controlled series of enzyme-catalysed steps that traps most of the energy in ATP, while combustion releases it all at once as heat and light.

distractorRationale.b: Both processes produce carbon dioxide when a carbon compound is oxidised
distractorRationale.c: Enzymes are biological catalysts and are involved in respiration, not combustion
distractorRationale.d: Combustion produces light; respiration does not

questions.stem: Bread dough rises before baking mainly because yeast

options.text: releases carbon dioxide that forms bubbles in the dough
releases oxygen that expands the dough
produces lactic acid that softens the gluten

questions.explanation: Yeast respires anaerobically on the sugars in the dough and releases carbon dioxide gas. The gas is trapped by the elastic gluten network and forms bubbles that expand the dough, while the ethanol produced alongside it evaporates during baking.

distractorRationale.a: Water absorption occurs during mixing and does not account for the rise
distractorRationale.c: Yeast consumes oxygen if any is present; it does not release it
distractorRationale.d: Lactic acid comes from bacteria and is not the cause of the rise

questions.stem: In which part of the cell does the aerobic stage of respiration take place?
questions.explanation: The first stage, glycolysis, occurs in the cytoplasm, but the oxygen-requiring reactions that release most of the energy occur inside the mitochondrion, on its folded inner membrane. Anaerobic respiration is confined to the cytoplasm.

distractorRationale.a: The nucleus contains chromosomes and controls the cell
distractorRationale.c: Chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis and occur only in plant cells
distractorRationale.d: Ribosomes synthesise proteins

questions.stem: Carbon dioxide is one of the products of anaerobic respiration in human muscle cells.
questions.explanation: False. Anaerobic respiration in muscle converts glucose to lactic acid only, with no gas released. Carbon dioxide is produced by anaerobic respiration in yeast, alongside ethanol, and by aerobic respiration in all cells.

questions.stem: Maize seeds sown in waterlogged soil often fail to germinate. The best explanation is that

options.text: the seeds absorb too much water and burst
water fills the air spaces, so the seeds respire anaerobically and release too little energy, while alcohol accumulates
the seeds are washed too deep into the soil
waterlogged soil has no mineral salts

questions.explanation: Germination is energy-hungry, and that energy comes from aerobic respiration of the stored food. When water fills the soil air spaces there is no oxygen, so the seed switches to anaerobic respiration, which releases only a small fraction of the energy and lets toxic ethanol build up.

distractorRationale.a: Seed coats are tough and seeds regulate water uptake; bursting is not the usual cause
distractorRationale.c: Depth is a separate planting issue and not caused by waterlogging
distractorRationale.d: Waterlogged soil still contains mineral salts, and germination depends on stored food, not soil minerals

questions.stem: Write word equations for aerobic respiration, anaerobic respiration in yeast and anaerobic respiration in muscle. State three economic uses of anaerobic respiration by micro-organisms.
markingGuide: Aerobic: glucose + oxygen gives carbon dioxide + water + energy (2 marks)
Yeast: glucose gives ethanol + carbon dioxide + energy (2 marks)
Muscle: glucose gives lactic acid + energy, with no carbon dioxide (2 marks)
Use 1: brewing of palm wine, burukutu or beer, and baking of bread, using yeast (1 mark)
Use 2: production of ogi, fufu, yoghurt or other fermented foods by lactic acid bacteria, which also preserves them (1 mark)
Use 3: treatment of sewage or production of biogas by anaerobic bacteria (1 mark)
Note that the anaerobic equations release far less energy than the aerobic one (1 mark)
questions.explanation: The three equations must be kept distinct, and in particular the muscle equation must not include carbon dioxide. The economic uses should name both the product and the organism responsible, since the mark is for the applied link rather than for the product alone.

questions.stem: Which of the following equations represents aerobic respiration?
questions.explanation: The correct equation for aerobic respiration shows glucose reacting with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide, water, and energy. This process occurs in the mitochondria of cells and is essential for efficient energy production.

distractorRationale.b: This equation represents anaerobic respiration in yeast, not aerobic respiration.
distractorRationale.c: This equation does not accurately depict either aerobic or anaerobic respiration.
distractorRationale.d: This equation is incorrect as it does not represent the complete aerobic respiration process.

questions.stem: What is the primary energy yield of aerobic respiration compared to anaerobic respiration?
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration yields approximately 36-38 ATP molecules per molecule of glucose, significantly more than the 2 ATP molecules produced during anaerobic respiration. This higher yield is due to the complete oxidation of glucose in the presence of oxygen.

distractorRationale.a: This value represents the ATP yield from anaerobic respiration.
distractorRationale.c: This is an inaccurate representation of the ATP yield from either type of respiration.
distractorRationale.d: While close, this option does not reflect the maximum yield, which is 36-38 ATP.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes fermentation?

options.text: A process that requires oxygen to produce energy.
A form of anaerobic respiration that produces alcohol or lactic acid.
A process that occurs only in plant cells.
A process that releases carbon dioxide and uses glucose.

questions.explanation: Fermentation is a type of anaerobic respiration that occurs in the absence of oxygen, leading to the production of substances like alcohol (in yeast) or lactic acid (in muscle cells). It is an essential process for organisms that live in environments lacking oxygen.

distractorRationale.a: This describes aerobic respiration, not fermentation.
distractorRationale.c: Fermentation occurs in both animal and plant cells, not exclusively in plants.
distractorRationale.d: While fermentation releases carbon dioxide, it does not use glucose in the same way as aerobic respiration.

distractorRationale.b: While carbon dioxide is produced in aerobic respiration, it is not a byproduct of anaerobic respiration in humans.
distractorRationale.d: Glucose is a substrate, not a byproduct, of anaerobic respiration.

distractorRationale.c: The nucleus is not involved in the process of glycolysis.
distractorRationale.d: The endoplasmic reticulum does not play a direct role in glycolysis.
